body:
## Summary

Four audit findings accepted in the 2026-08-03 `/decisions` session. Two of them (#215, #216) were
decided by Vlad on 2026-08-01 and implemented then; the other two (#233, #237) were prepared by the
nightly fix routine. All four were re-verified together in this session rather than trusted from
their recorded gates.

The four changes touch disjoint files and are independent of each other. They are separate commits
by intention.

## Changes

**`fix(procurement)`: internal warehouse moves no longer double-count as fulfillment (#216)**
`computeRemainingRequestedQty` / `computeFulfilledQty` had no `kind` filter, so a same-project
warehouse-to-warehouse move (a `kind: "stock"` order that goes straight to `received` carrying
`procurement_item_id`) was subtracted from `requiredQty` a second time for units a supplier order had
already counted. Decided option A: exclude same-project stock orders, keep counting cross-project
«in» transfers. The existing test at `procurement-fulfillment.test.ts:77` encoded the old behaviour
and is rewritten.

**`fix(procurement)`: the AI sidebar gets a real procurement context (#215, partial)**
`useProcurementReadProjectSummary` always returned `null` in Supabase mode, so the assistant answered
procurement questions from an empty picture with no signal anything was missing. Extracted
`buildProcurementReadProjectSummary` as a pure function and pointed the hook at the per-project
sources that already resolve every mode.

**~~`fix(tasks)`: #233~~ — REMOVED from this PR (`e7d4317`).** The prepared fix introduced a
blocking defect of its own and was pulled rather than patched again. `ProjectTasks.tsx` and
`ProjectTasks.test.tsx` are restored to their `origin/dev` state, so this PR does not touch task
completion at all. #233 is back in the decision queue with the finding recorded. See the round-3
section below.

**`fix(ai)`: Russian prompts match, and the fallback answers in the UI language (#237)**
Four English-only regexes meant none of the sidebar's own Russian chips could produce a proposal, and
the miss fell back to a hardcoded English array. Regexes extended with Russian stems; fallback moved
into the locale files behind `t()`.

## How to test

Staging, `https://vladosda0-rovno-90e7.twc1.net`, QA account.

1. **#237** — `/demo`, press «Купить материалы» unchanged. Expect a proposal card and Russian text.
   Repeat for «Добавить задачи», «Обновить смету», «Сгенерировать договор».
2. **#233** — open the Done prompt, attach one photo, force a failure (offline), confirm, restore
   network, confirm again. Expect one copy of the photo, not two.
3. **#216** — a procurement item with `requiredQty 100`, a received supplier order of 60, then a
   same-project warehouse move of 60. Expect 40 remaining in «Запрошено», not 0.
4. **#215** — open the AI sidebar on a Supabase project that has procurement rows and ask a
   procurement question. The context should no longer be empty. Home «Снабжение» stays blank; that
   is #267.

## Migrations / deploys included

None. Frontend only, no `supabase/migrations` and no `supabase/functions` changes, so no `cpush` and
no `cdeploy` follow this merge. Timeweb autodeploys `dev`.

## Risks

- **#216 moves a money figure upward.** Post-fix audit on 2026-08-01 found three readers the issue
  never named: `OrderModal.tsx:341,367` and `estimate-v2/rollups.ts:156`. `toBePaidPlannedCents` was
  UNDERSTATED by the same bug, so «к оплате» rises with this change. Correct, but user-visible.
- **#237 reclassifies FOUR chips, not two.** Corrected by the pre-merge audit: besides «Какие задачи
  в зоне риска?» and «Объясни отклонение по бюджету», the widened `смет` stem also catches
  «Сравнить сметы» (now yields an update_estimate proposal with the hardcoded 48,000 -> 52,000 ₽
  numbers instead of a text reply) and «Подбери материалы под смету» (matches both `материал` and
  `смет`, so it yields TWO proposals). All four are symmetric with the pre-existing English
  behaviour, and none can execute without an explicit per-item confirm, but the original "two
  residuals" claim in the commit message and in this body was wrong.
- #215 is partial by design. The Home «Снабжение» tab is still blank for every Supabase user; that
  half is #267 and it carries an architecture decision (client 4xN fan-out vs a portfolio RPC).

## Rollback

`git revert` any single commit — the four are independent and touch disjoint files.

## Checklist

- [x] `npm run verify` exit 0, measured on the branch WITH `origin/dev` (`67518d1`) merged in, i.e.
      on what actually lands: **182 test files, 1742 tests**, lint and typecheck clean.
      Node v22.22.3 locally, matching the version CI pins.
- [x] Each fix carries a test that was measured failing before and passing after, in the same
      environment (local vitest).
- [x] Handoff patches re-cut from the release worktree and verified to apply onto `origin/dev`
      @ `5be5045` before committing.
- [x] No file overlap between the four changes; applied in sequence with no fuzz.
- [ ] **No codex audit and no `/code-review` has run on any of these four yet** — no PR existed until
      now. Both gates run on this PR.

Closes #216
Closes #237
Refs #215, #233, #267, #275


---

## Pre-merge audit (2026-08-03)

codex: **silent (usage limit)** — it posted a quota comment, not a review, so the `/code-review`
subagent was the only gate.

`/code-review` (high) subagent: **FINDINGS — blocking=0 substantive=6 trivial=3.** It ran
`npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` and `npm test` itself (all pass, 177 files / 1683 tests) and read
31 files, 19 of them unchanged dependencies.

**The merge is blocked**: four findings need a design/scope decision and are not in-pipeline
auto-fixes. Two of them are defects in code THIS PR introduces:

1. **The #233 skip-list key omits the task id**, and the upload loop dereferences
   `doneUploadedKeysRef.current` at completion time. Closing the prompt mid-upload (the «Назад»
   button is not disabled during `doneUploading`, and the backdrop click is unconditional) and
   opening Done on another task installs a fresh Set that the still-running loop then writes into,
   so task B's prompt can start with a poisoned skip-list and B can complete with no `is_final` row.
2. **Resetting the skip-list on every prompt open leaves the original #233 defect reachable** via
   close-and-reopen on the SAME task, and the new test's stated rationale for that is false.
3. `useProcurementReadProjectSummary` drops `isLoading` and returns `null` while loading;
   `buildAIProjectContext` maps that to zeros, so the assistant can be told a project has no
   procurement. Narrower than the #215 defect it replaces, not absent.
4. `transferDirection === "in"` counts a merely-`placed` cross-project transfer as fulfilling a
   requirement. Byte-identical to pre-diff behaviour, but the new predicate is where the rule is now
   stated and its comment claims to state the whole rule.

Queued for the fix round once those are decided: the hardcoded English
`Using "<title>". Preparing proposals now.` at `AISidebar.tsx:1765` (the key
`ai.sidebar.message.usingProject` already exists in both locale files), plus three trivials (two dead
exports carrying the very defects this PR fixes, and one vacuous test).


---

## ⛔ Round 3 (post-fix) — merge blocked by a regression in the fix itself

A fresh `/code-review` on `6358a56` returned **blocking=1 substantive=4 trivial=1**. The blocking one
was INTRODUCED by `6358a56`:

Removing the reset-on-open made the skip-list permanent for the component's mount, and the residual
written into the code (`ProjectTasks.tsx:229-231`, "a remount clears the set") **is false** — the
photo-delete affordance is inside the same mount (`ProjectTasks:1047` -> `TaskDetailModal`
`projectMedia={media}` -> `PhotoViewer:63`). So: task done with photo P, P deleted, task reopened,
same file re-picked -> the upload is skipped and the task has **no `is_final` row**. On demo/local

body:
## What changed

- return the exact message IDs processed by bulk folder moves and keep failed moves reviewable
- add duplicate-group actions for Archive, Trash, custom folders, and optional future sender rules
- preload the reader, display mail before mark-read and inline-image work completes, and compress API responses
- remove redundant server-side HTML reparsing from every message open; import sanitization and client DOMPurify remain in place
- persist audit records after the response is sent instead of holding message requests open
- load duplicate-group members as summaries in one query instead of loading every full body and attachment list sequentially

## Why

The review workflow could not distinguish successful moves from failures. Duplicate detection offered no direct cleanup actions. Message opening also waited on secondary work and repeated expensive HTML parsing, while expanding a large duplicate group performed two database reads plus HTML parsing for every copy.

## Impact

Partial move failures remain reviewable, duplicate cleanup is available from the results screen, and message/detail views do substantially less work. Large email JSON responses are compressed, audit writes no longer delay the browser, and a group with 27 copies now uses one summary query rather than 27 full-message loads.

- `npm run typecheck --workspace @email-client/web`
- `npm run test:run --workspace @email-client/web` (29 files, 232 tests)

Doc-only. Appends §8 to the report-layer handoff and a pointer blockquote under its header.

## The problem

[2026-08-03-report-layer.md](docs/handoffs/2026-08-03-report-layer.md) §1.2 treats the 34-code spec backlog as claimed and cites **a live worktree** as the evidence: `claude/spec-backlog-producer`, at `075ad26`, with `docs/analysis/reproduce.py` modified.

That session finished while the handoff was in review. It merged as PR #47 at **21:17:11**, two and a half minutes before the handoff merged as PR #48 at **21:19:58**. The worktree is clean, the branch is gone, and the evidence §1.2 points at no longer exists.

The claim itself is fine, and its footing is now better: the backlog is claimed by a filed open work order, [2026-08-03-spec-backlog-producer.md](docs/handoffs/2026-08-03-spec-backlog-producer.md) (open, blocked on the Norgate producer, nothing to do in this repo), rather than by an in-flight tree. But a session that goes looking for the worktree will not find it, and "the claim expired" is the natural reading. That is the stale-marker failure this directory keeps recording, arriving from the opposite direction: `2026-08-03-index-share.md` sat marked open on top of finished analysis and invited a second execution.

## The fix

Appended as §8, not edited into §1.2. The body is preserved as issued, per the directory rule, and a pointer blockquote sits under the header so a reader hits it before §1.2. That is the pattern [2026-08-03-step2-contract-master.md](docs/handoffs/2026-08-03-step2-contract-master.md) already set.

This is **not an outcome section**. The handoff has not been executed and its status stays `open, unclaimed`.

## One finding carried forward

§8 also pulls `2026-08-03 §C15` into §2's field of view, because it is the same inference the gate has to make.

PR #47 raised an objection against its own work and withdrew it on measurement. ICE Europe WTI and the four Henry Hub codes look like variants of already-covered `CL` and `NG`, and open interest agrees (WTI at 0.771). But Managed Money net correlation is **negative in all five** (to −0.643) and week-to-week flow correlation is near zero, so they are a different holder base rather than a second copy. Reproducer `docs/analysis/reproduce.py::variant_codes_are_not_duplicates`.

The transferable part, and the reason it belongs in this handoff: **open interest is the series the eye reaches for when asking whether two things are the same market, and it is the wrong one, because crowding is a property of who holds.** §2 classifies caveats by whether a value exists that tells a reader the caveat applies. This changes the app from “serve source files directly from the repo root” to a TypeScript-based build workflow that emits a deployable site into `build/`. The migration keeps the existing static hosting model while introducing an explicit compilation and asset packaging step.

- **Build pipeline**
  - add `package.json` with TypeScript/esbuild-based build scripts
  - add `build.mjs` to compile browser entrypoints and assemble the deployable site
  - emit the built application into `build/` instead of serving source files in place
  - add `.nojekyll` in the output to avoid static hosting path issues

- **TypeScript source migration**
  - rename browser entrypoints from `.js` to `.ts`
  - add a minimal TypeScript config and ambient declarations needed for current browser/service worker globals
  - keep the migration low-friction by compiling the existing app structure rather than refactoring runtime behavior

- **Deployable asset layout**
  - copy runtime assets into `build/` alongside compiled scripts:
    - language data
    - puzzle data
    - styles
    - dictionary files
    - service worker
    - favicon
  - generate a built `index.html` that points at compiled module scripts under `build/src/`

- **Repository hygiene**
  - ignore generated output and installed packages from source control
  - keep the checked-in source tree focused on authoring inputs, with deployment artifacts produced by the build step

Example of the new workflow:

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "build": "node build.mjs",
    "typecheck": "tsc --project tsconfig.json"

}

<script type="module" defer src="src/game.js"></script>
<script type="module" defer src="src/index.js"></script>
```

External sync processes multiple versions, but marker cleanup currently returns immediately on the first failure. Versions later in the provider listing are never reconciled, and runtime links for versions that did succeed are not rebuilt.

For example, suppose nvm provides `node@18` and `node@22`, and the marker path for `node@18` cannot be removed because it is unexpectedly a directory:

$MISE_CACHE_DIR/node/18.0.0/incomplete/  # removal fails

author: pyth0n1c
body:
Better attack data archive with additional metadata and mapping functionality in the archive.


# Attack Data Archive Cache

This directory holds a local snapshot produced by `bin/build_dataset_archive.py`:
a Zstandard-compressed archive of the `datasets/` folder from
[splunk/attack_data](https://github.com/splunk/attack_data), plus two
standalone metadata files describing exactly what went into it.

This compression scheme ZIP + ZSTANDARD was intentionally chosen because:
- It provides very high compression and decompression ratios
- It is supported in Python3.14 without additional external tools or additional libraries
- The existence of individual files and extraction of individual files can occur without processing or extracting the entire archive. This makes extraction fast and minimizes disk usage on space-constrained runners (a fully decompressed attack_data datasets/ folder is approximately **11GB** at the time of this writing. The archive is **284MB.**
  - The size tradeoff here is that each file is compressed individually, such that replicated patterns across files are not optimally compressed. However, this tradeoff is a relatively small penalty and minimally increases the size of the archive. 
  - Re-extracting datasets that are re-used in multiple detections is a minimal penalty. ZSTD decompression is extremely fast, typically 100MB/s or 1000MB/s per core.

## Files

### `metadata.yml`
Summary of the archive build:

- `generated_at_utc` — when the archive was built
- `file_count` — total number of files included
- `gitref` — the exact commit hash the snapshot was built from
- `github_url` — link to the source branch/tag on GitHub
- `total_uncompressed_size_bytes` — combined size of all files before compression

### `url_to_file_mappings.yml`
Maps every file in the archive back to its source, split into two sections:

- `lfs-files` — a map keyed by the file's Git LFS download URL
  (`media.githubusercontent.com/...`), with:
  - `relative_path` — path within `datasets/`
  - `uncompressed_size` — size in bytes
  - `last-updated` — timestamp of the most recent commit that touched the file
- `non-lfs-files` — a flat list of relative paths for files stored directly
  in git (not LFS-tracked)

Use this file to fetch an individual dataset file directly from GitHub without
downloading the full archive.

## Notes

- Both files are also embedded inside the `.zip` archive itself, so they travel
  with it even if separated from these standalone copies.
- `gitref` in `metadata.yml` pins the exact commit; re-running the build script
  against a later commit will produce different contents even if `datasets/`
  is otherwise unchanged (e.g. `last-updated` timestamps).

body:
> Was stacked on #1109; that merged, so this is now **rebased onto `develop`** and targets it directly. Closes #1106, the last sub of epic #1103.

A contour with no number is a texture; with a number it is a map. CL2 put the level on the wire and marked the index-contour styles; this draws the numbers.

## The pass

Runs inside `render`, after the line pass and before every overlay, over the spans collect already decoded. Everything about it is shaped by the one constraint that outranks the design — **no noticeable frame time**:

- **No new I/O, no second decode.** The collect pass records a **6-byte candidate** (frame-point range + level) at the moment it publishes an index-contour winner — the one place the feature's `level` and its style's `contour_index()` flag are both in hand — so the label pass needs neither a span scan nor a style lookup. A side list rather than two more bytes on `Span`, which is 14 bytes × `MAX_SPANS` (1152); `MCU_RENDERER_BYTES` grows by **576 B** (96 × 6) and the 200 KB assert stays green.
- **One branch when there is nothing to label.** Empty candidate list ⇒ immediate return. That covers every map without terrain and every frame with the terrain layer hidden — #1096 gates the labels for free, since a suppressed style never leaves collect.
- **Bounded from above, twice.** `MAX_CONTOUR_LABELS = 12` stops the walk at the twelfth label, so a contour-dense frame does *less* per-candidate work, not more. And `MAX_ANCHORS_PER_LINE = 32` bounds one polyline's anchors — the stride is derived from the frame's m/px, and at a degenerate zoom it floors at a millimetre while a segment stays kilometres long, which is millions of rejected anchors and, past a wider ratio, an `f32` `next += stride` that is a no-op and never terminates. Thirty-two strides is ~5 700 px of line, far past what twelve labels need, so nothing reachable is truncated by it.

**Placement** (locked design): world-space arc-length cadence at `180 px × m/px`, the route-chevron precedent — anchors are ground spots, so they do not crawl under pan or rotation. Per-line phase is a **hash of the polyline's first vertex** (deterministic; no RNG, no clock, no frame counter), which stops parallel isolines stacking their labels into a column. Greedy first-fit against a fixed array of reserved boxes; a candidate that overlaps a reservation or would be clipped is skipped, never drawn clipped. Horizontal text on a parchment **knockout pill** — the bitmap tiers cannot rotate at any angle, and heading-up rotates the viewport.

**Two deviations from the issue text, both deliberate:**

1. **The pill colour comes from the host palette (`set_label_colors`), not from the scene.** My first cut painted it in `backdrop_style()` — which on grimsel is the **sea**: the shipped presets put water at the bottom of the paint order and paint land over it, so the pill knocked a blue hole in a mountainside. The map has no colour that means "the ground here", so the label — which is chrome, the same chip idiom as the status strip — takes paper and ink from the palette. Defaults are black on white, the pair the all-zero `init_zeroed` renderer can express; the app sets `PARCHMENT` + `CONTOUR`.
2. **`set_label_insets(top, bottom)` — a chrome keep-out.** The Map screen's clock and scale bar float over the map plane and are drawn *after* it, so a label under either was overwritten mid-glyph and read as a different elevation. This is the pass's existing "never clip a number" rule extended from the viewport edge to the area the map actually owns. The renderer is told a band, not a widget; the app derives the two numbers from the constants that place those widgets.

Ink is the locked design's `palette::CONTOUR` grey — legible on parchment in the sim; the `palette::INK` A/B is below for the on-glass pick (#1097).

## Perf

Three measurements, `obc-bench`, min-of-10 per scene, `--repeat 3/5` for the totals (same machine, quiet).

**A. This branch against the *unmodified* fixture — what the label pass costs when there is nothing to label.**

| scene | base (µs) | this branch, old fixture (µs) | hash |
| :-- | --: | --: | :-- |
| riding | 119 | 120 | **identical** |
| riding-rot | 154 | 156 | **identical** |
| mid | 106 | 102 | **identical** |
| mid-rot | 159 | 154 | **identical** |
| overview | 497 | 488 | **identical** |
| overview-rot | 497 | 500 | **identical** |
| route | 121 | 118 | **identical** |

All seven frame hashes reproduce byte for byte, and the deltas are inside the ±5 µs run-to-run spread. That is the pixel-identity proof the issue asks for: a scene with no index contours renders exactly as before.

**B. With the fixture now carrying labelled contours** — why the hashes are re-pinned. The bench map had no contour at all, so the label path would otherwise have gone unmeasured forever.

| scene | collect | sort | draw | **label** | total | labels |
| :-- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| riding | 12 | 0 | 118 | **2** | 133 | 1 |
| riding-rot | 12 | 0 | 143 | **4** | 160 | 2 |
| mid | 36 | 2 | 87 | **6** | 132 | 3 |
| mid-rot | 57 | 5 | 130 | **10** | 203 | 5 |
| overview | 297 | 15 | 195 | **0** | 507 | 0 |
| overview-rot | 297 | 16 | 202 | **0** | 515 | 0 |
| route | 37 | 2 | 85 | **6** | 145 | 3 |

≈ **2 µs per label** — one rect fill plus ~1.2 k glyph pixels, the irreducible cost of drawing a number. The rest of the delta versus table A is the extra contour *geometry* the fixture now carries, not the labels.

The overview pair reports **0**: contours ship at `priority: 4`, and that scene saturates the frame budget (2 684 of 3 708 features dropped), so the terrain layer is shed before the label pass ever sees it. That is the honest device behaviour, and it matches the real map too — at 30 m/px you are far coarser than LOD 2, where contours stop existing at all.

**C. A real map** (`obc-bench --map apps/obc-sim/assets/grimsel.obcm --mpp N`):

| m/px | LOD | labels | label µs | total µs | share |
| --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| 16 | 2 | 6 | 14 | 327 | 4.3 % |
| 13 | 2 | 7 | 14 | 251 | 5.6 % |
| 9 | 3 | 3 | 7 | 277 | 2.5 % |
| 4 | 4 | 2 | 4 | 279 | 1.4 % |
| 2 | 5 | 2 | 4 | 206 | 1.9 % |

The 12-label cap is never reached on a real map; 6–7 at planning zoom is what the terrain offers.

`RenderStats` gains `label_us` and `contour_labels`, and `obc-bench` prints both as columns — the numbers #1097's on-glass check will want.

## Board cost

`462,376 → 462,968 B` resident on both board profiles (CI's `embedded` guard caught it; the baseline commit is the fix, reproduced locally on both profiles). One allocation entry moves and the accounting is exact, with no linker slack: `renderer` 92,324 → 92,912 (+588), which `App`'s align-8 rounds to `app` 136,560 → 137,152 (+592), and `App` is the resident static.

The 588 is the 580 B candidate list (96 × 6 B + a 4 B length) plus 8 B for the label's paper, ink and chrome bands — four `u16`s that pack with the existing `suppress_terrain` bool into the 12 B where that bool alone took 4. No new static, no second buffer, no frame growth; `.data`, `.uninit` and the guarded poll frame are unmoved. Flash +3,488 B per profile, re-pinned from this PR's own `embedded` run.

Grimsel, headless sim, true colour. Reproduce:

  --zoom 13.7 --png planning-13mpp.png            # ~13 m/px, LOD 2, 5 labels

Independent of the other open PRs — targets `main`.

**Sweep eight**, over `itemRefById` — the resolver that answers *"what is this id?"*. The properties panel and the message panel both branch on its answer, so a kind it can't resolve renders as **two empty panels**: the item selects, and then tells you nothing about itself.

A sheet pin was that kind. Its id is `<sheetRefId>:sheetpin<k>`, there was no branch for it, and `itemRefById` returned `null` — even though `'sheetpin'` has been in the `ItemRef` union since #198 made pins first-class.

### Two changes

- `itemRefById` resolves sheet pins, validating the sheet **and** the pin index rather than trusting the shape of the string.
- `getMsgPanelItems` grows a `'sheetpin'` arm. `SCH_SHEET_PIN` is a `SCH_LABEL_BASE`, so it shows the name and shape a hierarchical label shows.

### The guard is the durable part

The sweep enumerates `ItemRef['kind']` and **fails when a kind has no case**. An unresolved kind is invisible in the UI — no error, no fallback, just blank panels — so it must not be possible to add one silently. `'table'` is excluded *explicitly with its reason* (its fixture needs a full `(table …)` node with cells) rather than quietly absent.

One test also pins down that a junction correctly shows **nothing**, so that emptiness stays deliberate — `EDA_ITEM`'s base `GetMsgPanelInfo` really is empty.

### Not fixed here — and this is the honest part

Both panels are thin well beyond this. `schPropertiesFor` handles **8 of 15** kinds and `getMsgPanelItems` **5**, each defaulting to `[]`.

Some of those are genuinely empty upstream. Bus entries, images, graphics, tables and directive labels are **not** — they have real `GetMsgPanelInfo` implementations. I've sized that in #195 rather than half-filling eleven arms in a PR about something else.

### Mutation-checked

Removing the `sheetpin` branch fails **3 of 19**. Confirmed failing, then restored.
